sections.heading: C — Yielding to pedestrians and visually impaired people, school zones, bicyclists' rights and bike lanes, giving motorcycles room, and commercial vehicle no zones
sections.markdown:
## C — Yielding to pedestrians and visually impaired people, school zones, bicyclists' rights and bike lanes, giving motorcycles room, and commercial vehicle no zones
Knowledge domain: how a South Carolina driver shares the road with pedestrians, including visually impaired people and children, with bicyclists, who count as vehicles, with motorcyclists, who need a full lane and a bigger gap, and with large commercial vehicles and their no zones.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Always be prepared to yield to pedestrians, even when they are not in a crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
You must yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk even if it is unmarked, and that includes mid-block crosswalks shown by warning signs and pavement markings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
You must always yield the right-of-way to visually impaired people, and you must come to a complete stop when a pedestrian crosses guided by a dog or carrying a white cane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Yield the right-of-way to every pedestrian in the intersection, even when your light is green. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A02
When turning right on red, be ready to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A02
Beside parked or stopped vehicles, pedestrians can step out between them, so slow down and do not pass a stopped vehicle until you are sure no one is crossing in front of it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
Before backing up, check for pedestrians in your path, especially in parking lots and other busy pedestrian areas. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
In playground and residential areas children may run out from between parked vehicles, so it is wise to drive below the speed limit there and be ready to stop quickly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
In a school zone you must obey the lower speed limit when its lights are flashing or children are present, and at a school crossing with a traffic patrol you stop and yield if signaled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
On the road a bicycle counts as a vehicle, so bicyclists must follow the same rules of the road and have the same rights, privileges and responsibilities as motorists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A03
A skillful bicyclist rides predictably in a steady line, while an unskillful one may swerve, ignore signs and signals or ride at night without a light, so be ready for sudden moves. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A03
Yield to bicyclists in intersections just as you would to pedestrians and other vehicles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A03
Yield where a bike path or lane crosses a road, and do not stop, park or drive in a bike lane unless entering or leaving an alley or driveway, on official duty, directed by police or in an emergency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A03
Give a bicyclist as much room as possible and slow down when approaching or passing, and let the cyclist clear the intersection before you make your turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A03
Avoid slowing down or stopping suddenly near a bicyclist, because a motor vehicle's brakes are stronger than a bicycle's and you could cause a collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A03
Do not sound your horn close to a bicyclist unless a collision is possible, since the noise can startle the rider into steering into your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A04
Watch for bicyclists moving into your lane, and take special care when children ride on the sidewalk, because they may come onto the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A04
Do not turn sharply in front of a bicyclist, and never force one off the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A04
Bicyclists are required to ride with the direction of traffic, but you should still look for them anywhere on the roadway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A04
Be extra careful around bicyclists on wet roads or roads covered with sand or gravel, which affect bicycles far more than cars. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A04
Bicyclists must use hand signals to turn and stop, but some may not know them or may need both hands on the handlebars, so watch for clues such as a head turn or a look over the shoulder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A05
When parked on the street, check the sides and rear for bicyclists before you open your door. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A05
Motorcyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers, but they can be harder to see. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A05
Give a motorcycle a full lane width and do not share the lane, because the rider needs that space to react to traffic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A06
Motorcycles are small and hard to see, so remember they are part of traffic and always check your mirrors and blind spots for them. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A06
Before turning left, look carefully to the front and sides of your vehicle for motorcycles. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A07
Do not assume a motorcycle is turning just because its signal is flashing, since motorcycle signals may not cancel themselves; wait until you are sure the rider is turning. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A07
Follow a motorcycle by at least 4 seconds, and by more in wet conditions, or you may lack the time and space to avoid a collision. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A07
Riders may suddenly change speed or lane position to avoid hazards such as gravel, potholes, railroad crossings, grooved pavement, pavement seams and wet or slippery surfaces, any of which can be deadly to them. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A07
The manual reports more than 250,000 collisions between cars and commercial vehicles each year, many of which could be avoided. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A07
Commercial vehicles are larger and harder to maneuver than cars, have much larger blind spots, need longer distances to stop and speed up, and need more room to turn. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A08
The no zone is the area around large trucks and buses where other vehicles disappear from the driver's view, with blind spots at the sides, rear and front. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A08
Side no zones are big on both sides of large trucks and buses, and a truck's right-side blind spot starts behind the cab and can extend the length of the truck. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A08
If you cannot see the truck driver's face in the side view mirror, the driver cannot see you. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A08
Never stay alongside a large vehicle longer than you must, because if its driver has to swerve or change lanes the chance of a collision rises sharply. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0116]

Misconceptions: a green light does not end your duty to yield to pedestrians in the intersection; an unmarked crosswalk is still a crosswalk; a bicyclist is a vehicle with the same rights as a car; a flashing motorcycle signal may be left on by mistake; if you cannot see a truck driver's face in the mirror, the driver cannot see you.
Mnemonics: white cane or guide dog means a full stop; bikes are vehicles, motorcycles get the whole lane; four seconds behind a motorcycle, more when wet; no face in the mirror, no view of you.
Glossary: mid-block crosswalk means a crosswalk between intersections marked by signs and pavement markings; bike lane means a lane designated for bicycles; no zone means the blind-spot area around a large truck or bus; commercial vehicle means a generally larger, less maneuverable vehicle such as a large truck or bus.
Dynamic facts: the yearly count of collisions between cars and commercial vehicles is a statistic that changes over time; refresh it before it is shown.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
